payoutReward(address,uint256).details: Pitfall: this function **silently truncates** on insufficient balance (pays the full balance instead of reverting) -- this is so a user's claim   is not blocked by a short-term treasury shortage; but the caller **must** use the return value to detect underpayment, otherwise an underpaid entitlement is unobservable.

convertFistdaoFeeToOskLp(uint256).details: Full path (the 5 hops of `_burnFistdaoWithFist` **in reverse order**, with identical pair dependencies):        FISTDAO -> BNI -> WBNB -> USDT -> FIST      then reuse `_fistHalfToOskLp`: FIST split in half -> half buys OSK via OSK/FIST -> form LP -> insurance pool.      Caller: **anyone can call it directly** (keeper-driven) -- the funding source is the tax passively transferred in on FISTDAO transfers      (FISTDAO.oskPool wired to this contract), with no trigger fee; isomorphic to NodePoolDistributor. Pitfall (severe): **this contract** must be added to the whitelist on the FISTDAO side -- otherwise when this contract transfers FISTDAO   into the pair it triggers FISTDAO's 3% sell tax (the router internally does transferFrom -> not whitelisted -> taxed),   making the deposited amount differ from expectations. Pitfall: the amount comes from "this contract's FISTDAO balance" rather than an argument -- the tax accumulates passively, so the caller need not compute the amount,   and it also avoids a lingering remainder. Pitfall: reverts when not wired (fistdao/bni/usdt/fist/oskFistPair), never silently trading on a wrong path. Pitfall: this function carries transientNonReentrant -- so it must **not** be called internally from other guarded functions of this contract (it would self-lock).   The caller must be an **external call chain** (a keeper script / operational multisig).

injectFistToOskLp(uint256,uint256).details: **The landing point after the client change on 2026-09-26**: the 2% fuel fee for FIST staking is now charged in **FIST itself**,      so this function becomes that fuel fee's landing path (the original `injectOskToOskFistLp` direction is thereby disabled).      Caller: `CoreVault` (`stakeB` in `Contracts/CoreVaultStaking.sol` = FIST staking). Design intent: the fuel fee is first transferred into this contract, which completes the swap + addLiquidity; LP goes to the insurance pool,           so CoreVault need not hold a router dependency. Pitfall: measure OSK by the "actual received delta", never trusting the router's quote array -- a token with a transfer tax makes the quote exceed the actual receipt. Pitfall: reverts when not wired (fist/oskFistPair), never silently trading on a wrong path.

injectOskToOskFistLp(uint256,uint256).details: WARNING: **no longer on the requirements path**: on 2026-09-26 the client changed the FIST staking fuel fee from "opposite OSK"      to "same-token FIST", with the landing point moved to `injectFistToOskLp`; so "OSK fuel fee -> form LP" has no caller.      Reason for keeping: ABI alignment with deployed instances + historical traceability; it must **not** be wired to any requirements path. Pitfall: measure FIST by the "actual received delta", never trusting the router's quote array. Pitfall: reverts when not wired (fist/oskFistPair), never silently trading on a wrong path. Pitfall: direct on the OSK/FIST pair (user statement: OSK has only the OSK/FIST pair).

params.token: token address (ERC20, or address(0) for native BNB)

pullFromInsurancePool(address,uint256).details: Pulled directly via InsurancePool.withdrawReserve, with no approve needed

swapOskToFistAndInject(uint256,uint256).details: Path: OSK -> FIST **direct two hops** (the OSK/FIST pair already exists, no need to route via USDT).      Caller: CoreVault (the 2.5% withdrawal tax drawn at farming claim time). Pitfall: must be direct rather than OSK->USDT->FIST -- going via USDT pays an extra fee and introduces extra slippage;       and Requirement 2.0 L144 states OSK has only the OSK/FIST pair, no USDT/OSK pair exists,       so the original three-hop path would revert directly on the real chain due to the missing pair. Pitfall: measure FIST by the "actual received delta", never trusting the router's quote array -- if FIST has a transfer tax,       the quote would exceed the actual receipt, and transferring based on it would revert for insufficient balance. Pitfall: OSK always completes the swap while staying in the Treasury, never held by an intermediate contract, so assets are not lost on failure. Pitfall: reverts when not wired (oskFistPair/fist/fistStakingPool), never silently trading on a wrong path.

allocateFistDeposit(address,uint256,uint.details: Requirement 2.0 section 2:   |- 10% FIST = FIST->USDT->WBNB->BNI->FISTDAO then burned directly after buying   |- 20% FIST = insurance pool multisig address (FIST reserve, redemption reserve + automatic market-making)   |- 70% FIST = split in half: 35% FIST->OSK (direct on the OSK/FIST pair), 35% FIST retained                -> OSK + FIST automatically add LP, LP sent to the insurance pool address Design intent: the caller (CoreVault) first safeTransfers the FIST into this contract, then calls this function;           everything is measured by the "actual received balance delta", never trusting the router's quote array. Pitfall: reverts when not wired (any of usdt/fist/fistdao/bni/oskFistPair is 0),       never silently trading on a wrong path -- a fund-allocation error costs far more than a failed trade. Pitfall: callable only by FarmVault, preventing any address from bypassing CoreVault's position and referral logic.

aPair.details: Requirement 2.0 L144: the A-side pair = OSK/FIST (OSK has only this pair).      Used for refill (_refillFromPair) and the ratio window; the quote side = FIST, no longer WBNB.

fistUsdtPair.details: FIST/USDT pair -- **this pair is not registered with the Pancake factory** (it is actually deployed on FstSwap on mainnet),      so `PancakeRouter.getAmountsOut`/`swap` cannot route it (the router only knows its own factory's pairs).      Every swap crossing USDT<->FIST must go through `_pairHop` directly on this pair. Pitfall: validate the direction when wiring (token0/token1 = one of USDT/FIST) -- a direction mismatch would reverse the swap arguments,      an unrecoverable fund misallocation.

MAX_REFILL_IMPACT_BP.details: The **upper bound** on the A-coin drawn from the pair per refill (BP, 1e4 precision). Design rationale (user-specified): restored to **5%** -- i.e. `aR / 20`, consistent with the original implementation.   Measured on the mainnet test build: each claim draws 5.996e24 OSK (exactly 5.00% of the reserves). Pitfall (known side effect, not a defect): a single 5% draw pushes the OSK relative price up by about 5%,   making `aPerB`/`aPerUsd` jump -> the tier hit drifts accordingly (measured effective tR 252 -> 74 -> 78).   That side effect has been largely mitigated by the "three-source median" oracle (OracleLib._selectPrice3):   the median filters out single-point outlier prices, so the tier no longer destabilizes from a single refill. Pitfall: the bound must be based on the **reserve proportion** rather than an absolute amount -- an absolute amount becomes too large an impact once the reserves shrink.
